content.content:
Apply these criteria to the dependent's recorded decision node and the implementation artifacts its ref names, reading them against the prerequisite in both directions; nothing runs. A placeholder or unrefined decision node, or an artifact that leaves the prerequisite unenforced, fails naming the missing or diverging part.

(1) Necessity: the prerequisite states in prose that selection emphasis must be expressed so that dimming or brightening elements adds no per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element presentation, compositing, paint, layout, style-recalculation or traversal work when the viewport moves or scales, leaving the interaction and stylesheet artifacts to settle the concrete representation. The dependent must depend on the prerequisite, commit in its recorded rationale to how its selection emphasis expression holds that bound across a viewport change, and enforce that expression in its referenced artifacts. Fail if the dependency edge, the rationale's account of the emphasis representation, or the artifact enforcement is absent or could be dropped without loss, naming the gap.

(2) Fidelity — LOOSER (the artifact permits per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element work on a viewport change): the dependent's artifacts must enforce every part of the prerequisite's commitment across the full cost of a viewport change under active selection emphasis, from the viewport-change input through the viewport-transform update and all host style-recalculation, layout, paint and compositing work through to the displayed surface.
- (a) Passive emphasis representation: both the dimming of unselected elements and the brightening or highlighting of selected and related elements must be expressed exclusively through presentation properties that settle when selection changes and remain passive while the viewport moves or scales — in the already-rendered appearance of the affected elements (such as their resolved fill, stroke, border, outline or text colors) or in a fixed number of shared layers that does not grow with the dimmed or brightened set. Fail if the artifacts express dimming or brightening on each dimmed or brightened element through per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element compositing groups, per-element opacity or filter stacking surfaces, per-element blend passes, or styles and attributes that the host must re-evaluate, repaint, blend or recomposite per dimmed or brightened element when an ancestor viewport transform changes — naming the diverging rule or declaration and `looser`.
- (b) Viewport-change path: when the viewport moves or scales under active selection emphasis, the viewer's own code must neither walk, query, re-class, restyle nor update the dimmed or brightened elements, nor invalidate or refresh selection emphasis as part of applying the viewport transform. Fail if any viewport-change path traverses or updates the dimmed or brightened set or provokes per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element style recalculation, layout, paint or compositing work — naming the diverging path and `looser`.

(3) Fidelity — STRICTER or smuggled rules (the artifact over-restricts, trades away interactivity, or substitutes a different goal): the dependent's rationale and artifacts must enforce no stricter rule and smuggle in nothing the prerequisite does not license. Fail if the dependent substitutes a frame-rate target, latency budget, or element-count or node-count ceiling or threshold; if it throttles, coalesces away, skips or drops viewport updates; if it suppresses, clears or degrades active selection emphasis during or across viewport changes to avoid viewport-change cost; or if it introduces an unrecorded rendering host, library, protocol or file outside its scope — naming the diverging rule or element and `stricter`.
content.rationale: The prerequisite mntwwzyl is inline prose at the natural layer committing how selection emphasis is expressed across a viewport change, and the dependent noplrntp is a code-layer implementation whose ref names the interaction modules and stylesheet, so the edge sits in the evaluation matrix's natural-to-code cell and takes the fidelity form: the prose leaves the concrete emphasis representation to the code-layer artifacts, and those artifacts together with the dependent's recorded rationale must enforce what the prose claims in both directions, neither looser nor stricter, with nothing smuggled in. Because the prerequisite's commitment is about the full cost of a viewport change under active selection emphasis through to the displayed surface, a check that looked only at whether viewport updates write a single transform or whether selection changes write classes incrementally would miss the host presentation and compositing cost that per-element emphasis primitives incur on every pan or zoom. The looser direction therefore checks both that viewport changes do not walk or rewrite the emphasized elements and that dimming and brightening are expressed through passive resolved-appearance properties or a fixed number of shared layers rather than per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element compositing groups, opacity or filter stacking surfaces, or blend passes. The stricter direction checks that the bound is met by how selection emphasis is expressed rather than by throttling or dropping viewport updates, suppressing emphasis during pan or zoom, or smuggling in a latency, frame-rate or element-count threshold. The criterion names no selector, class, function or property literal of the dependent in advance, so it survives any rewording or refactoring of noplrntp that preserves the same behavior and emphasis expression; specific offending rules or gaps appear only in the check's output.
